climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.
climb.window_rationale: Fixed at W = 117 by the sweep rule preregistered in phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1 before that run, whose three deciding predictions held. W = 134 measured slightly higher on indel draws there; the rule forbids choosing it on that evidence.
climb.first_plug_rationale: Partial exhaustion of the first plug (Ostwald and Weierud 2017, section 7, the 'E-Stecker' method): the climb is run from the empty plugboard and from each of the 25 boards that plug E to another letter, and the best final n-gram score is kept, the earliest board winning a tie. Without it the climb is v4's exactly (the empty board is the first start). The reason is docs/code-review-2026-10-11.md B-1: the repository's power controls used one plaintext of IC 0.0792, Army traffic averages about 0.061, and detection falls steeply with plaintext IC because the first climb phase is an index-of-coincidence climb that traps. 26 starts cost 26 times the climbs.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

limitations: The controls are constructed or independently solved plaintexts, not authentic held-out Army traffic with an authentic daily key.

The messages behind the published 1941 n-gram counts are not enumerated, so overlap between the authentic control plaintexts and the scorer's training data cannot be ruled out. The constructed control exists to bound that risk, not to remove it.

The positive controls are body-direct and are handed the true wheel order, ring setting and start positions. They certify the stecker stage at the target lengths and say nothing about the rotor enumeration, which the sweeps and calibrations cover separately.

Every result assumes UKW-B, the Army/Air Force wheels I-V and the 1940+ clear-Grundstellung indicator procedure. A different reflector, a Naval wheel or a different indicator convention is outside every space searched here.
The calibrations use one plaintext per cell and a single key draw per cell. They locate the detection boundary to within a cell, not to a precise length.

The authentic control pools five short messages under one daily key (275 letters); the constructed control pools three at the target lengths (371 letters). Neither certifies a single 167-letter message on its own, which is what the capability calibration measures.

The middle-complete space has an exact equivalent for every daily key at 167 letters (rule_key_coverage 1.0). A key is still found only if the climb converges at one of its equivalents and scores into the top 100 of nine times as many settings as v3 searched; the stated power measures the first on planted draws and stands in for the second with a pooled null.

Companion confirmation for the E arm has not been measured. The earlier middle-past-notch calibration and v5 confirmation fraction cannot certify the middle-complete E-arm check at typical plaintext IC; the extrapolation is labelled as inference in stated_power.
No result here is an accepted break: a confirmed candidate's plaintext still has to be read and reviewed before accepted_break could change.

The E-arm detection is measured on clean and single-indel 167-letter draws around planted keys, against that arm's own pooled wrong-setting null. Top-100 retention over all 246,767,040 settings and the far tail of the E-start null are not measured by the control.

The sweep scores each setting by the better of two 117-letter windows, so its scores are not on the scale of v2's whole-message scores; the indicator confirmation, which compares a pooled date score with the candidate's own sweep score, is reported but is even less informative here than in v2. The companion check alone decides.
A candidate found through the tail window is reported at the setting that deciphers the tail, which for a garbled message is one keystroke away from the setting of the head.

This power is unconditional across the new plaintext/key draws. Conditional companion-confirmed power given all four prior sweep arms missed is unmeasured; no additional posterior odds multiplier is calibrated for v6.
The prior probability of a dropped or inserted letter is unmeasured. Keep clean and one-indel rates separate; any mixture or borrowed confirmation rate is an explicit inference.

The cited paper (Sullivan and Weierud 2005, footnote 42) places Batch C on a different radio network and its authors suspect differently wired wheels. Every figure here assumes wheels I-V as wired; if that is wrong the power is zero and a null says nothing about these messages.

The choice of E-Stecker follows the 2026-10-11 preregistered P2/P3 launch rule, both passed by its control. Earlier split-point yield models used a different plaintext and CPU engine and do not establish current E-Stecker efficiency.

The E-arm control measured clean and single-indel draws only. V6 spends extra cost on first-plug starts, retains W=117 head-and-tail windows, and does not test a combined E/split search, two faults or substitution-specific E-arm power.

The stated power comes from Markov plaintexts of the scorer's own counts, not authentic held-out Army traffic, and from a slice around a planted key, not the whole space; the E-start null (the best of 26 climbs) is heavier-tailed than the whole-message one, so the 6-sigma detection threshold of the control and the z = 6 companion threshold of the sweep are not the same quantity.

The 480 key draws reuse 24 plaintexts. The reported Wilson interval describes pooled key-draw variability and does not include uncertainty over the language model, plaintext distribution or real target traffic. P2 passed by 3/480 draws; its interval includes values below 75%.

refuted_by: Any failed prerequisite, preflight, positive control, exception, first-run incomplete slice or resumed settings_run greater than zero refutes operational readiness on this host; target candidate scores are not a decoding result.

body_direct_sweep.rationale: Same message, ring rule (middle_complete), climb (W = 117), retention, start axes, right-ring axis, companions and threshold as v4, run on the cuda engine from the start; the only change is climb.first_plug = E. v4's 246,767,040 settings are swept again with 26 start boards each. Projected cost: v4 took 33 minutes on the RTX 3090, so about 14 hours (26 times; an inference to be replaced by the measured figure). 1,560 checkpointed chunks, so a stop loses at most one chunk.

predictions.statement: At least one of the 100 retained candidates is companion-confirmed (min over FKQLZ and XFEDT of best-start z >= 6).
If a candidate is confirmed, it is also the sweep's rank-1 candidate on BYQMZ alone.

Re-climbing each of v4's 100 retained settings with the E start set gives a score per letter at least v4's, to within 1e-9. The empty board is the first start and the climb from it is v4's exactly, so a fall would mean the implementation changed the climb. Checked after the run by a CPU re-climb of v4's retained rows.
All 100 retained candidates re-climb identically on the CPU batched climber (plugboard and score), as v5's did on the CPU SplitClimber.

If no candidate is confirmed, the sweep's top score lies between z = 5.5 and z = 8.0 over the distribution of all 246,767,040 settings' scores (v4 6.51). The upper bound is higher than v4's preregistered 7.5 because the best of 26 climbs has a heavier right tail than one.
